name: Osborne Reef

sources.title: Osborne Reef — artificial reef off Fort Lauderdale, first of concrete jacks, enlarged with scrap tyres in the 1970s
Nova Southeastern University, Horizons (2007) — the tyres cover more than 34 acres in 60-70 ft, about 1.3 miles off Fort Lauderdale beach
Florida DEP — Osborne Reef waste tire removal project: one to two million tyres put in the ocean in the 1970s
Oceana (2006) — Florida officials to corals: our bad

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q1272680_osborne_reef.py, tools/meshkit.py, tools/scenekit.py) with AI assistance. About 250 m of the tyre field at about 20 m: some 8,500 tyres drawn as a sample of the hundreds of thousands still there, loose and drifted, heaped up against the edge of the natural reef to the east, with a few bundles still tied and patches cleared by the removal work; the old concrete jacks at its heart. The layout and the number of tyres are approximate. No marine life in the model: Offlined draws the living things itself.
